text:
Noah P.: Quick question — I'm on parental leave now and my next RSU vesting date is during my leave. Does time on paid parental leave count toward service for vesting and performance bonus eligibility? Also if I take a partial unpaid extension, how does that affect cliff/acceleration rules?

Sofia (People Ops): Short answer: paid parental leave counts as active service for vesting and bonus eligibility. Unpaid extensions can be trickier. I'll loop in Riley from Comp and Equity-Admin for specifics.

Riley (Comp): Hi Noah 97a Our standard plan doc states: "All periods of Company-approved paid parental leave shall be treated as continuous service for purposes of time-based equity vesting and performance bonus eligibility." So your paid leave week counts.

Riley (Comp): For unpaid extensions: generally unpaid leave beyond the paid entitlement pauses service-based vesting unless prior exception is approved. Exceptions are case-by-case and need sign-off from Comp + People Ops + Legal.

Noah P.: Thanks. If the unpaid extension pauses vesting, does that shift the vesting date forward by the exact length of the unpaid period?

Equity-Admin: Yes — if unpaid leave causes a service interruption, we adjust the vesting schedule forward by the number of days of non-service. You'll see an updated vesting calendar in Carta/Equity portal after HR confirms.

Noah P.: OK. Any effect on the 90-day post-termination exercise window for options if I transition to a contractor or leave the company while on leave?

Legal-Bot: Options exercise windows are governed by your grant agreement. Generally, termination for any reason (resignation, termination) triggers the post-termination exercise window from the termination date. Being on leave doesn't extend that window automatically. If you're converting to contractor, we need to check grant terms and possibly get an amendment.

Riley (Comp): Also note performance bonus eligibility: if you're on paid parental leave during the performance period, you remain eligible and payout is pro-rated by time worked in the performance period only if the plan defines pro-rata. For Redwood's FY performance plan, paid leave counts as time worked for eligibility; payout uses actual FTE during the review period.

Noah P.: Is the parental top-up considered "compensation" for equity calculations or bonus calculations? (i.e., will top-up dollars count toward target bonus or equity refresh eligibility?)

Riley (Comp): Parental top-up is treated as a leave benefit, not salary, so it does not increase base salary for future target bonus calculations. It does not count as performance-eligible compensation for the annual bonus. Equity refresh eligibility is based on active headcount/service and base salary banding; the top-up itself doesn't change banding.

Sofia (People Ops): Practical next steps: 1) If you think you might extend unpaid, file a leave amendment form and cc Comp + Equity-Admin. 2) If you want an official vesting projection now, reply "vest-proj" and @Equity-Admin will send the updated calendar.

Noah P.: vest-proj please. And can you confirm whether parental leave accruals (like service accrual for tenure-based perks) continue while on paid leave?

Equity-Admin: Received. We'll send a vesting projection.

Riley (Comp): Tenure accruals for perks follow the same service treatment: paid parental leave counts toward tenure-based eligibility (e.g., sabbatical, long-service awards). Unpaid breaks may pause accruals unless approved otherwise.

Noah P.: Awesome, thanks folks. Filing the amendment now just in case. Appreciate the quick clarifications. :clap:

Sofia (People Ops): Happy to help. Ping if you want us to loop Legal for an amendment template.

Equity-Admin: Sent the projection to your inbox (subject: "Vesting projection - Noah P.").
_notes: Discusses RSU vesting, paid vs unpaid parental leave effects on service, bonus eligibility, option exercise windows, and next steps. Includes informal Slack tone with a call-to-action 'vest-proj'.
